players.product: Recursion OS, biological foundation models, and Lab-in-the-Loop drug engine

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results release (8-K Exhibit 99.1): total revenue, consisting primarily of collaboration revenue, was $7.7 million vs $19.2 million in Q2 2025; Roche and Genentech revenue was lower because certain project phases were completed in the prior period. R&D expenses fell to $89.6 million from $128.6 million, primarily on lower platform costs from the timing of Tempus record purchases and improved operating efficiency.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 total revenue $7.7 million vs $19.2 million; R&D expenses $89.6 million vs $128.6 million

quarterly_data.signal: Platform scale stated in the August 2026 corporate presentation (8-K Exhibit 99.2): 300M+ experiments, 2M+ samples sequenced, 340M real-world patient lives and 50+ petabytes of multimodal data generated by automated labs; 100 million+ molecules generated per year with synthetically aware design and ~90% of synthesized molecules AI-generated, scored and prioritized; >10 development candidates designed across programs. Recursion says its TxFM foundation model outperforms 16 competing models while trained on 100x less data.
quarterly_data.figure: 300M+ experiments; 340M real-world patient lives; 100 million+ molecules generated per year; ~90% of synthesized molecules AI-generated; >10 development candidates; TxFM vs 16 competing models on 100x less data

quarterly_data.signal: Supplier Tempus AI (data license to Recursion): Q2 2026 results release (8-K Exhibit 99.1): Recursion's R&D expense included $3.1 million of non-cash expenses for the use of Tempus' patient-centric multimodal oncology data within its R&D pipeline in Q2 2026, compared with $22.7 million in Q2 2025, reflecting the timing of Tempus record purchases.
quarterly_data.figure: patient-centric multimodal oncology data records; $3.1 million non-cash expense in Q2 2026 vs $22.7 million in Q2 2025

connects_to.relationship: AI-discovered neuroscience targets and joint drug discovery

contracts.signal: Q2 2026 results release and decks (8-K Exhibits 99.1-99.3): Genentech exercised the first Validated Target Option under the neuroscience collaboration (deck: 1st target optioned 3Q26, $3M), advancing a previously unexplored neuroscience target into a small molecule early discovery program; Recursion has achieved $216 million in upfront and milestone payments from the Roche and Genentech collaboration to date. The collaboration includes up to 40 potential small molecule discovery programs, each with potential for more than $300 million in development, commercialization and net sales milestones plus tiered royalties up to high single digits.
